# Visual direction and raster assets

This reference supports mock exploration and raster asset production on any coding model with suitable tools. The filename is retained for compatibility. Read it when the requested work benefits from imagery; the presence of an image tool does not make generation a prerequisite for implementation.

## Establish or reuse a direction

Start from the brief and existing design contract. Reuse an approved palette, mock, reference, or delegated direction. Ask a focused question only when an unresolved visual decision materially affects the result. A user-requested checkpoint still applies; prior approval does not expire just because the task moves from planning to assets.

For a requested exploration, create a small set of alternatives sufficient to resolve the visual choice. A palette artifact is useful when palette is the actual open question. Otherwise go directly to the requested mock or asset. Keep mock variants consistent on approved choices and vary meaningful structure, hierarchy, density, or composition.

Show the relevant result. Obtain a selection when the user reserved that decision; choose and explain it when selection was delegated. Do not silently replace an approved hero composition or other major ingredient. Stop iterating when the decision is resolved or a missing input blocks it.

## Translate a mock into implementation

Inventory its major ingredients: hero silhouette, section sequence, navigation and actions, imagery, typography, materials, and distinctive motifs. For each, choose semantic HTML/CSS/SVG, an existing asset, generated or sourced raster, an installed icon, or canvas/WebGL. Record an accepted omission when needed.

Keep core content, text, controls, and navigation semantic and accessible. Treat the mock as a visual direction rather than a single flattened image of the page. Preserve the approved composition and required image-native content; do not replace a photographic or product-led concept with generic CSS scenery or filler cards.

## Produce assets

For each required raster asset, establish:

- Reference or selected mock and the ingredient to reproduce.
- Output location, dimensions, format, and transparency requirements.
- Elements to preserve or avoid, and what remains semantic UI.

Use the current harness's image tools and existing permissions. Use real, generated, or sourced imagery according to the brief and available capabilities. Do not ask the user to install a generation service merely to follow this reference. If a required capability is missing, report the specific asset that remains blocked and proceed with independent work.

Asset production may be delegated when delegation is available, authorized, and useful; otherwise handle it in the current task. No named subagent is required. Give any delegate the same bounded brief and permitted output paths.

Inspect the resulting assets, keep required files in the project, and verify their paths. Check dimensions, crop, transparency, meaningful alternative text, and performance costs in context. Keep private material out of external prompts or uploads without authorization covering that use.

Return to [craft.md](craft.md) to implement and verify the feature. Report any accepted change from the chosen direction and any missing asset evidence.
